newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA AVERAGE ONE-WEEK RATE UP TO 70.05 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA AVERAGE ONE-WEEK RATE UP TO 70.05 PCT.

text.p: The average rate for Romania's central bank's one-week funds rose to 70.05 percent at this week's refinancing auction from 65 percent in a previous session, central bank data showed on Friday.

The central bank (BNR) offer of 750 billion lei, down from a previous 1.1 trillion, was slightly oversubscribed with two banks entering bids totaling 777 billion lei at prices ranging from 70 to 71.5 percent.
The central bank has recently tightened its monetary policies in a move to calm down a soaring inflation and in line with International Monetary Fund recommendations.
On Thursday the BNR raised the minimum permitted rate for one-week funds by five percentage points to 70 percent, after jacking up that rate to 65 percent from 57 last week.
Year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent last December, far above the 20 percent target agreed with the IMF for 1996.
An IMF mission is now in Bucharest to discuss a new loan accord with the centrist coalition government which emerged from last November's elections. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
